data.narrative:
Harmattan AI, a Series B-stage defense and security frontier-tech company, is evaluated against a peer universe of 10 comparable companies: 2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms spanning the same sector and stage.

Two valuation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the company's $1.4B last post-money valuation, implying $2.7B. Peer-median benchmarking examines five same-sector, same-stage comparables (Dream Security at $3.0B, Code Metal at $1.2B, Defense Unicorns at $1.0B, Heven AeroTech at $1.0B, and TurbineOne at $300M), yielding a median of $1.0B and a range of $300M to $3.0B. The peer set reflects material dispersion in Series B defense-tech valuations.

Triangulation across these two methods supports a valuation range of $850M to $3.1B, with a median of $1.8B. Harmattan's current $1.4B valuation sits below the triangulated median, positioning it within the lower-middle quartile of the peer range. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the five-company peer sample, execution risk at Series B, and near-term capital deployment efficiency relative to peer benchmarks. The wide range ($300M–$3.0B among peers) signals material heterogeneity in stage-comparable risk profiles and growth trajectories within defense-tech.
